name: graph-first-navigation
body:
The codebase-navigator's ""graph first"" rule is an explicit procedural ordering that applies to ANY question about code or structure — discovery and enumeration included (""what is in this file?"", ""what does this unit depend on?"", ""what are the frontends?"") — and to relationship claims (callers/callees/uses/containment). For every such question the FIRST tool call is a graph query; `read`/`grep`/`glob` are confirmatory — they open the `path` a graph result returned, at its `start_line`/`end_line` — or they read artifacts the graph omits. The rule names both artifact classes.

`opencode-suite/agents/codebase-navigator.md` rule 1 (""Graph first, then file read"") states the ordering for ANY code/structure question, discovery and enumeration included, and names both classes (the in-graph list and the exclusion list). `AGENTS.md` carries the same qualifier in its ""Other tools"" section and on the ""Read those files with read, grep, or bash"" line; `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md` rule 5 requires every generated agent to inherit the ordering; and the coherence test `rust.apg.tests.e2e.graph_first_rule_stated_in_navigator_prompt_and_guide` (`src/main.rs:5147-5275`) asserts both.

The artifact-class boundary follows the bundled structural scanner's coverage of every tracked text/config/packaging file:
- In the graph: all scanned source (`src/**`), scanned Markdown (`AGENTS.md`/`README.md`, `opencode-suite/**`), and every tracked text/config/packaging file the structural scanner claims — `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` (toml), `install.sh` (sh), `.github/workflows/release.yml` (yaml), `apg/config.json` and `opencode-suite/package.json` (json), `LICENSE` (misc).
- Out of the graph: ZERO SYMBOLS, meaning a `File` node with zero Module/Struct/Function facts — Ruby sources (`Formula/*.rb`, pending `apg-ruby`) and binaries have zero frontend, so they appear only as residual `misc` `File` nodes. The genuinely unclaimed paths — zero node at all — are those the config scope (`apg/config.json`) and the standard exclusions (`.git`, `target`, `node_modules`, `.gitignore`, `--exclude-path`) remove.

Acceptance criteria:
- The installed navigator prompt's rule 1 carries an exclusion list meaning ""ZERO SYMBOLS, with a `File` node present"" — Ruby sources (pending `apg-ruby`) and binaries are residual `misc` `File` nodes with zero Struct/Function facts, and the genuinely unclaimed paths are those the config scope and standard exclusions remove — while its in-graph list names the tracked text/config/packaging files the structural scanner claims. The ordering and the dual-class shape hold.
- `AGENTS.md` carries the corresponding exclusion list; the graph-first qualifier it carries stays.
- `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md` rule 5 requires every generated agent to inherit the graph-first ordering.
- The coherence test `rust.apg.tests.e2e.graph_first_rule_stated_in_navigator_prompt_and_guide` (`src/main.rs:5147-5275`) passes; a pinned shrunk list lands its assertions in that same test.
- The observable goal is behavioural: an agent answering a discovery question queries the graph before reaching for a file tool, and knows the tracked text/config/packaging files are in the graph.
